requirements.text: Define a linear transformation as a function that maps vectors to vectors while preserving two key properties: addition (T(u+v) = T(u)+T(v)) and scalar multiplication (T(cu) = cT(u)). requirements.text: Introduce the core insight: To fully describe a linear transformation, you only need to know where the basis vectors i-hat and j-hat end up. Since any vector is a combination of i-hat and j-hat, if you know the new locations of the basis vectors, you know where every other vector goes. This reduces an infinite amount of information to just four numbers.

requirements.text: Connect the geometric movement to algebraic notation. Explain that the matrix is simply a container for the coordinates of the new basis vectors.
